principle: Ask Interface Designer for visual expertise only when it materially improves the video. Return a presentation decision package to Video Editor; never transfer editorial or renderer authority.

VISUAL_DIRECTION.when: A substantial graphic language, typography, palette, composition system, or project visual identity must be created or changed.

include: representative frames or stills when useful

forbidden: change EDL or editorial cut decisions

REFERENCE_RECREATION.when: A supplied screenshot, website, reel, frame sequence, design reference, or named visual target should influence the look.

include: Video Editor's timestamped editorial/reference observations when they exist
exclude: claims that uninspected audio was heard
permission to copy branded assets without rights
permission to replace editorial pacing analysis

forbidden: infer or claim audio-reference facts from silent frames
declare final reference match without rendered evidence

PROTOTYPE_VISUAL_DIRECTIONS.when: A meaningful motion-graphic identity decision is ambiguous, the user asks for options, or choosing a direction before building the entire edit reduces rework.

include: one bounded beat or representative frame/section
exclude: authority to rewrite the editorial message

forbidden: change spoken meaning or edit order
treat a prototype as final rendered acceptance

MOTION_TASTE.when: Rendered graphic motion needs specialist taste on pacing, easing, continuity, emphasis, gesture, or interaction-derived motion principles.

include: reduced-motion or accessibility constraints when relevant
exclude: permission to stretch beat timing beyond editorial anchors without Video Editor approval

forbidden: override HyperFrames timing or adapter rules
change caption or transcript timing truth
